items.title: Drops for Nvidia, Anthropic and other AI stocks drag the markets back down
items.summary_auto: Stocks tied to the  artificial intelligence industry dragged the U.S. market lower Tuesday after their surge from the day before quickly fizzled.

items.title: Alberta government backtracks, won't make schools install secondary flag poles
items.summary_auto: The Alberta government is backtracking on recently announced flagpole regulations, now saying schools will not need two poles to fly both the provincial and Canadian flags outside.

items.title: U.S. jury finds Chinese tech giant Huawei guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets
items.summary_auto: A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.

items.title: Stellantis taking Unifor to court over obstruction of environmental work
items.summary_auto: The ongoing dispute over the sale of Stellantis' Brampton, Ont., assembly plant is heading to court, as the automaker has filed a lawsuit alleging Unifor is impeding an environmental assessment necessary to the transaction.

items.title: Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music from its platform
items.summary_auto: Tidal announced Tuesday it is banning fully AI-generated music from its platform, marking one of the toughest stances a major streaming platform has made against the influx of AI tracks in recent years.

items.title: 'Crypto King' was actually at gas station when he testified alleged kidnappers waterboarded him elsewhere
items.summary_auto: The self-described 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski was at a gas station east of Toronto at the same time he previously testified he was being waterboarded about a two-hour drive away, the jury at the trial for his alleged kidnappers heard Tuesday.

items.title: Use of physical restraints on seniors at N.L. care homes is more than double national average: report
items.summary_auto: The third volume of a now annual report from the provincial seniors' advocate highlights how seniors in Newfoundland and Labrador are doing across six key indicators.

items.title: Innu leaders cry foul over use of force in Sheshatshiu arrest; RCMP says man had weapon
items.summary_auto: Harry Dyke was arrested Saturday night after police received a report of a disturbance involving a weapon, RCMP say.

items.title: Zosia Mamet says Mad Men creator made set 'absolutely horrible'
items.summary_auto: Despite its storied run, Mad Men had an 'absolutely horrible' on-set vibe, says actor Zosia Mamet, which pushed her to drop out of a recurring role.

items.title: Minister defends 2027 permanent residency plan, says 'vast majority' are already in Canada
items.summary_auto: Immigration Minister Lena Diab says the federal government is managing newcomers responsibly as the Conservative Opposition seeks to block a plan that could see as many as 662,000 people receive permanent residency next year.

items.title: Smart watches, AI glasses now outlawed in Manitoba schools
items.summary_auto: Smart glasses, smart watches and other wearable technologies are now included in the ban on cellphones in schools that has been in place since September 2024, says the Manitoba government.

items.title: Despite 'glitch,' BepiColombo spacecraft reaches Mercury after 8 years, space agency says
items.summary_auto: The European Space Agency said on Monday the BepiColombo European-Japanese mission to explore Mercury is "on track" and the spacecraft is safe despite a glitch that occurred when it began orbiting the solar system's smallest and innermost planet.

items.title: Bank of Canada expects 2nd round of oil-linked inflation in 2027, Macklem says
items.summary_auto: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem sees high energy prices continuing to sting consumers at the fuel pump and beyond in 2027, even as oil prices fall from recent peaks.

items.title: Rudy Giuliani awarded Presidential Medal of Freedom a year after being pardoned for potential crimes
items.summary_auto: Rudolph Giuliani, the former New York City mayor and longtime ally of President Donald Trump, was honoured on Tuesday with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, which comes after several years of personal legal peril.

items.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'deeply shocked' after nude images from her rape case used in book promotion
items.summary_auto: Gisèle Pelicot says she is deeply shocked that a Paris publishing house used nude images taken of her by her rapist ex-husband as promotional materials for a book that examines her watershed fight for justice.

items.title: Alberta pushes back against federal hate speech law that removed religious exemption
items.summary_auto: Alberta’s government is planning to introduce a motion under the province’s Sovereignty Act targeting the federal government’s recent anti-hate legislation.

items.title: $5K bonus payments for trades workers going out early next month, government says
items.summary_auto: Bonuses for Red Seal trades workers are set to be delivered starting early next month.

items.title: 3 human cases of avian flu confirmed in Washington state, including a death: WHO
items.summary_auto: The World Health Organization said on Tuesday it had been notified by the United States of three confirmed human cases of bird flu in Washington state, including one death.

items.title: Anthem singer apologizes for botched O Canada lyrics at Leafs game against Islanders
items.summary_auto: The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to the Canadian national anthem.

items.title: U2 announces 2027 shows in Toronto, Vancouver as part of world tour
items.summary_auto: U2 announced the first Canadian dates in its world tour on Tuesday, in support of the new album Carnaval de Luz.

items.title: Spike in emissions a major setback in GTA climate goals: report
items.summary_auto: A more polluting energy grid and rising demand for gas heating during a colder winter drove the largest annual spike in planet-warming emissions in at least a decade across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, a new report found, putting the region further off track of its climate goals.

items.title: 2 men arrested after break-in at country residence of Prince William, Princess of Wales
items.summary_auto: British police said Tuesday that two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate. It follows reports that the home of Prince William and Princess Catherine on the vast royal estate was broken into on Monday.

items.title: Mortgage delinquency rate up 31% in third quarter: Equifax report
items.summary_auto: Equifax Canada's third-quarter consumer credit trends report says the national 90-plus day mortgage delinquency rate — defined as missed payments three months in a row — reached 0.32 per cent, the highest since the credit agency started tracking the metric in 2013.

items.title: Heat waves are getting so bad that even this cactus can't survive
items.summary_auto: Despite evolving for millennia to thrive in the blazing Sonoran Desert, the iconic saguaro cactus is struggling to survive escalating heat waves.

items.title: Top civil servant in N.L. fisheries department also travelled on aquaculture company’s dime
items.summary_auto: The Legislative Standards Commissioner, Ann Chafe, is doubling down on her approval of a study trip to Scotland for Fisheries Minister Loyola O'Driscoll and his department's top civil servant Keith Sullivan. The travel was educational and "deemed to be in the best interest of the public," says a statement from Chafe's department on Tuesday.

items.title: Regina transit lockout ends after tentative deal reached
items.summary_auto: The transit worker lockout is over in Regina after the city and Amalgamated Transit Union (ATU) Local 588 reached a tentative three-year agreement late Monday evening.

items.title: Building water bombers or growing crops? This Alberta county has cast its vote
items.summary_auto: An Alberta farmer who used to rent 600 hectares of cropland west of Strathmore, Alta., is now reckoning with the land being turned into De Havilland's new aircraft manufacturing and commercial site, which will build coveted water bombers, but also take the place of some of the province's most productive soil.

items.title: Steelhead struggling in B.C., while some salmon species see small improvements: report
items.summary_auto: Pacific salmon in B.C. and the Yukon remain in a "precarious" state, according to the third annual State of Salmon report by the Pacific Salmon Foundation.

items.title: Private diaries of Pope Francis reveal spiritual crisis and visions of the devil
items.summary_auto: The late Pope Francis suffered a two-year spiritual crisis starting in 2021 when he felt tempted by the devil and struggled with how to wield power over the Catholic Church, a new collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday revealed.

items.title: Anti-immigration group’s tour of the Maritimes draws criticism
items.summary_auto: The Dominion Society made stops in Charlottetown, Fredericton and Halifax trying to attract new members. Some local residents say there’s no room in the Maritimes for the group’s message of division.

items.title: A teenage runaway turned to a Mountie for sanctuary. He had other plans
items.summary_auto: Kim Budd spent much of her childhood on the run. When she thought she'd finally found a safe place to stay it turned out to be anything but, and the adults and institutions that were supposed to protect her failed her when she needed them most.

items.title: Wildfire victim trying to buy new Flin Flon, Man., home loses $170K in lawyer impersonation scam
items.summary_auto: Five Manitobans in the last two months have fallen victim to a fraud scheme where scammers infiltrate lawyers' emails and redirect money. One woman in Flin Flon, trying to buy a new home after losing hers in a wildfire, is out more than $170,000.

items.title: Montreal's 'unprecedented' tax hike key to tackling 'infrastructure crisis,' mayor says
items.summary_auto: The City of Montreal unveiled its newest budget and it comes with a major tax hike that represents a broken campaign promise from the mayor.

items.title: Ottawa proposes sweeping new land-seizure powers for Alto high-speed rail project
items.summary_auto: The federal government is proposing to scrap standard expropriation rules for Canada's first high-speed rail project.

items.title: Health Canada seizes peptides from Toronto shop, warns of health risks of unregulated market
items.summary_auto: Health Canada confirmed it confiscated and is now testing a number of what it called "unauthorized injectable peptides" from the shop, Not Peptides.

items.title: Quebec grocery store believed to be oldest in North America revived with an Italian twist
items.summary_auto: Quebec City's J.A. Moisan is believed to be the oldest grocery store in North America. It has survived great depressions and uncertain times, but it’s ready for a new beginning once more. New tenants promise to honour the founding family's legacy, but with an Italian twist.

items.title: Why Trump's move to get Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO won't end the questions
items.summary_auto: U.S. President Donald Trump's extraordinary intervention to get Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO does little to shut down many pressing questions about a scandal that has rocked both Washington and the stock markets.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI lets you buy flowers for your girlfriend. Some streamers say it's too woke
items.summary_auto: The new Grand Theft Auto VI brings old classics back to the franchise, but this iteration also has some changes. Instead of hiring sex workers, the early part of the game has you doing chores for your in-game girlfriend, like buying her flowers and fixing the leak in the roof.

items.title: 'Brexit means Brexit' no more? Why the U.K. now wants closer ties with the EU
items.summary_auto: Brexit might not have meant Brexit after all. At least, the door to a "Breturn," as they’re already calling it here, has been nudged open a crack or two by Britain’s Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

items.title: Ontario nurses at a breaking point share stories of stress and burnout in a new report
items.summary_auto: A new report shares first-hand testimonies from Ontario nurses who describe enduring burnout, anxiety and distress working in understaffed and under-resourced hospitals in the province. The report's co-author says it's meant to shed light on the realities facing the profession.

items.title: Trump administration blacklists Megaspeed cloud company linked to Nvidia scandal
items.summary_auto: The U.S. Commerce Department on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed, the cloud company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist following criticism from lawmakers and administration officials.

items.title: Alleged Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator asks court to revoke detention order
items.summary_auto: According to court filings, Melody Bryant was not the only one who initially failed to recognize killer Jesse Van Rootselaar was "genuinely dangerous." The motion says records show the shooter shared her plans widely and had even "received encouragement from other online contacts."

items.title: 'I'm not a hero,' says Arizona man who found lost toddler alone in the desert
items.summary_auto: Search parties with helicopters, K-9 units and heat-seeking drones scoured the rural dessert community of Eloy, Ariz. for hours looking two-year-old Vella Campillo after she wandered away from her backyard — all to no avail. Then Jay Stewart found her hiding in a bush.

items.title: Rights group details 'surge' in violent attacks on Palestinian health-care workers
items.summary_auto: Based on testimony from health-care workers, Physicians for Human Rights Israel says there’s been a 350 per cent increase in violence against Palestinian health workers by settlers and the Israeli military. Israel denies the report's claims.

items.title: 11-year-old Carly Rae Jepsen song surges up the charts thanks to GTA VI needle drop
items.summary_auto: Justin Bieber, Tate McRae, April Wine and other acts are also featured in the game.

items.title: Carly Rae Jepsen sees streaming surge after GTA VI needledrop
items.summary_auto: Justin Bieber, Tate McRae, April Wine and other acts are also featured in the game.
